title: the sages
hook: the third book opens in a clearing full of old ascetics, and the first thing they ask a prince in bark clothes is to be their king
carry: you are our king, protect us

segments.voice: Yesterday: the sandals, part two. Bharata set them on the throne at Nandigrama, and the second book closed with Anasuya's gifts to Sita. Did you do something for someone who wasn't there? Today, the third book: the Aranya Kanda, the book of the forest. Day five hundred fifty.

Aranya means forest. And the forest Rama walks into now is Dandaka, the great wild country south of everything he knows. It's not empty. The first thing he sees, Valmiki says, is a ring of hermitages: little huts, fires burning for the daily offerings, grass laid out for rites, deer wandering without fear, birds everywhere. Old men and women with matted hair look up from their prayers. And they come out to meet him.
screen: `ARANYA: THE FOREST.` → `DANDAKA, THE WILD SOUTH.` → `A RING OF HERMITAGES.`

segments.voice: The sages see Rama, Valmiki says, and can't stop looking at him: his build, his calm, his beauty, the bark clothes he wears like a king's robes. They bring fruit and roots and water, and give the three travelers a hut to rest in. And then they say something surprising. You are our king, they tell him. Whether you live in a city or in the forest, you are still the king, and a king is the one who protects. We've given up the rod of punishment ourselves. We've given up anger. We live by our austerities. So we're like children in your care. Protect us. Notice what they're saying. Rama has just been stripped of the crown in Ayodhya. His brother is ruling through a pair of sandals. And here, in the forest, the first people he meets hand the title straight back to him. Not the palace, not the throne, but the duty. In the sages' own words, a king is the one who protects. The sages have chosen a life without weapons. Someone has to stand between them and the dark. Hold onto that request. Much of the forest book grows out of it: the battles, the promises, even the danger that will come to Sita. It starts here, with old people in a clearing, asking a young man in bark clothes to be what he was born for.
screen: `THEY CAN'T STOP LOOKING.` · `YOU ARE OUR KING, CITY OR FOREST.` · `WE'VE GIVEN UP THE ROD.` · `PROTECT US.` · then, large: `THE CROWN COMES BACK AS A DUTY.`

segments.voice: Sit comfortably and let the breath slow. Picture a clearing in a forest: small fires, quiet people, birds. Now think of someone in your own life who is in some way in your care, someone who relies on you to stand between them and trouble. Let their face come clearly. Breathe in steadiness. Breathe out calm. You don't have to solve anything for them right now. Just notice that they're in your care. The bell holds the time.
The sages. The forest ascetics of Dandaka welcome Rama and ask him, king or not, to be their protector.
Your line: you are our king, protect us. Today, notice one person who quietly relies on you, and show up for them. Day five hundred fifty.

howItsDone: The Aranya Kanda, the book of the forest, opens with the sages' welcome in Dandaka, and their plea for protection runs through the book.

original.note: Sanskrit daṇḍakāraṇya: the forest (araṇya) of Daṇḍaka, the wild country where most of the third book happens.

trapdoor: what you thought: Rama goes into the forest to be alone.
what it means: he walks into a forest full of hermits who need a protector.
what a scholar hears: Aranya 1 has the sages name Rama king and protector even in exile, and the theme of protecting the hermits runs through the whole book.
